Rhino Orphans

By: Graham Coetzer | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Unexpected Bedfellows: At a secret location in the middle of the South African bush, we meet the most unexpected of bedfellows, Mpho and Flenters. One is an orphaned rhino calf, the other a sheep. The

Unique Selling Point:
We have behind the scenes access to the Rhino Orphanage - a non profit organisation that saves orphaned rhinos, often after their mother's fell victim to poachers. Young rhino are completely incapable of caring for themselves if they lose their mother's, and will either fall prey to predators such as lions or eat dirt in an attempt to survive, which will lead to a tragic death.

The Rhino Orphanage specialises in saving these orphans - they have trained K9's who can track the animals, and dedicated carers who work around the clock to keep them alive when they're first brought in. One such case happened in June this year, when they saved their latest addition, Mpho. Because Mpho is still too young to be placed with other rhinos, and they don't want her to get too used to humans, she's been given a companion animal - Flenter's the sheep. The two are getting along like a house on fire, and with Flenter's help Mpho should one day be able to return to the bush.

Summary:
Mpho and Flenters are the stars of our show - and we'll focus on getting amazing footage of their unique bond. As their story unwinds, we'll meet all the role players behind the orphanage, find out how they started, and why they do what they do.

There are many other orphans to meet - quite a few of them named after Springbok rugby players. Each with their own tale of tragedy turned healing.

One such Rhino calf is Impi, who will be having a specially fabricated prosthetic leg fitted while we are there. Impi and his mother spent two days fighting off a pride of lions before they were saved. Both were badly injured during the encounter. No one is sure if the prosthetic will work, but we'll capture the moment.

While the scourge of rhino poaching is a devastating reality in South Africa, and one we won't ignore in the insert, this story is really about Mpho and Flenters, and in true South African tradition, about how the most diverse of backgrounds can lead to inspiring friendships.

Further information:
We have been granted access to everything and everyone at the orphanage, and they are happy to help.
I have agreed not to disclose the location.

Extra Budget Items:
Crew will travel together in my car.
It is apparently about a four hour drive from Johannesburg. Last bit of the road and getting to the farm roads are bad.
I want to request that crew perhaps sleep over two nights? Otherwise we will have very limited time for filming. Half day at best on day 1 and would have to leave by about 3/4pm second day. i will request a quote for one night accommodation and two.
Other issue is the only nearby place to stay is a group called Entabeni Mountain Lodge, with two venues called Lakeside and Kingfisher. Everything else will involve a lot of traveling. I will get quotes.

Rhino Orphans
First Draft Script
27 Nov 2023

INTRO

On Screen Text - “Somewhere in the African bush…” Car drives over text

Link Macfarlane in car
So this is quite a rough road, but that is to be expected, because we’re going to a secret location somewhere in the bush. And we’re going to meet two very special friends - and in true South African style, they both come from diverse backgrounds…

Voice
It’s a story of triumph over tragedy … in an unexpected location … kept secret …from organised crime. 
But just like the unusual friends we’ve come to meet, it’s a place of resilience… 

ACT 1 - MPHO, FLENTERS AND THE ORPHANAGE

UPS
Gate opens, enter Mpho and Flenters

Voice
Meet Mpho and Flenters. Mpho is a five-month-old rhino orphan. Flenters a crazy Pedi sheep … and superstar rhino nanny. They’re besties. 

Upsound Arrie van Deventer
Arrie: She keeps Mpho company. And she’s a freaking character, you’ve seen her, she thinks she runs the place, she’s the queen bee here.

Mac: Well she’s always letting us know that she’s here right?

Arrie: Yes, yes

Mac: The minute she hears us its Bleh the whole time!

Arrie: Ja, the whole time, ja no she’s the queen bee.

On Screen text “Earlier” While Mac is in an interview Flenters bleats

UPS Macfarlane
Flenters: Baa

Mac: That’s Flenters, have you heard of Flenters?

Werner: Ja, he’s quite a popular one here

Flenters: Baa

Mac: Ja we coming, relax, your interview’s coming, chill (laughs)

Voice
The story of this extraordinary relationship…and their friends … starts with a magical place called the Rhino Orphanage - the home of a not-for-profit organisation founded by Arrie van Deventer.

Ups Arrie van Deventer
Arrie: And then you’ve got the three here, this is Thula, this is the blind one that I told you about and then we’ve got Kolisi on the other side.

Mac: And you’ve got Charlie over here

Arrie: We’ve got Charles Glass here.

Voice
All but one of the rhinos are orphans - most rescued by Arrie and his team when they were still too young to defend themselves.

UPS Mac
So gentle, so beautiful, wow.

Voice
Rhino calves are only weaned around eighteen months to two years - they may remain with their mother for up to three years. 
When the mother is poached - orphaned calves are helpless… easy prey.

UPS Arrie
Arrie: The youngest calf we ever had was four hours old.

Mac: Four hours old?

Arrie: Four hours after birth, the mother was shot.

Voice
With horns going for thousands of dollars a kilo on the black market, an estimated 10,000 rhinos have been lost to poachers in South Africa since 2007. 
Arrie couldn’t stand the carnage.

UPS Arrie
Arrie: Little Nandi came in she had 21 axe and panga wounds in her face and in her head, where the poachers were hacking her while they were hacking the mother’s face off. When I fetched her from Kruger National Park, the vet Markus Hofmeyer said to me we rather have to euthanise her and I said no while there’s breath, there’s life, there’s hope. And she’s now a big rhino.

Voice
It takes a lot of hope, and even more heart, to care for orphans like Mpho. 
They’re social beings, and since she’s too small to join the other rhinos, Flenters is her companion animal. 

They even share a bed - when they’re not eating it.

ACT 2 - A day in the life, Rugby, Kolisi and the prosthetic, other world firsts.

UPS Yolandé
Mac: So I found the nursery, this is where the babies get looked after. Hi Yolandé

Yolandé: Hi Mac

Mac: How are you?

Yolandé: Good and yourself

Mac: Lekker man, getting the milk ready for the babies?

Yolandé: Getting milk ready for the babies.

Voice
Yolandé van der Merwe is the orphanage’s head caregiver - it takes a team of six substitute rhino moms’ to keep hungry mouths fed. And dish out scratches. 

UPS Yolandé MPHO scratch

Voice
The latest orphan to arrive - five-month-old Mahlatsi… needs to be bottle-fed a specially prepared milk mixture every three hours. Already weighing in at a hefty 200kgs,  Mahlatsi will gain a kilo of body weight every day during her first year of life.

UPS Yolandé
Mac: 1 kilogram a day?

Yolandé: In their first year, yes.

Mac: That happens to my stomach once in a while…

Yolandé: Ja I know I get that too…

Voice
Older orphans are free to roam the surrounding private nature reserve. 

Some of these weigh upwards of a ton - no wonder they’re called a crash of rhinos.

UPS MAC
It’s a tough job out here hey, out in the middle of nowhere, feeding rhinos. Sho! But it’s much better than “kind regards”.

Voice
The middle of nowhere is not QUITE WHERE you’d expect to meet some celebrity sports stars…

UPS MAC 
Makazole Mapimpi! Hello baby!

Voice
The Springbok winger wasn’t the only surprise rugby-fanatic Arrie had up his sleeve…


UPS Arrie
I gave Kolisi his name when he came in there and he was in so much pain.

Voice
Four-year-old Kolisi arrived as a few-month-old with horrific injuries to his right rear foot from a hyena attack.

UPS Arrie
The first person I thought about was Siya Kolisi, I mean he’s our Captain Braveheart, if you see where he came from. Like I said he went to rugby trials and he didn’t have rugby shorts. This one came here and he didn’t have a foot.

Voice
Today Kolisi is fit and healthy, although he’s been crippled for life. For a young bull who weighs in at about a ton - that’s a problem.

UPS Arrie at Kolisi
Arrie: If you look at the Kolisi, you see the right back foot?

Mac: Yes.

Arrie: He keeps it up. That is the foot that was eaten by the hyenas when he was a baby.

Voice
For major medical problems, Arrie GETS A LITTLE help from his friends… Like “The Rhino Whisperer”.

UPS Dr Pierre Bester
Pierre: So we have to just trim the nails, so it fits in…

Mac: Oh, it going to feel like a “mani”?

Pierre: HAHA ja he’s going to have a manicure! 

Mac: Lovely.

Voice
Wildlife vet Dr Pierre Bester has earned his reputation. When rhino calf Duane Vermeulen was at death’s door from a blood-borne disease, Pierre saved his life by performing the world’s first-ever successful rhino-to-rhino blood transfusion.

AND fitting Kolisi with HIS specially designed moon boot - it’s all in a day’s work.

Ups Dart Kolisi
Mac: Quite a delicate process where he gets darted so as the Doc said to immobilise him.

Voice
Once the tranquiliser TAKES effect, the team WORKS quickly. But not before the human rhino moms have to show their mettle.

UPS Carers fend off charging rhinos

UPS Roll Kolisi over

Mac: That was like being in a scrum with Siya Kolisi… Steady, steady… Crouch, touch, engage!

Voice
Before his new boot can be fitted, Kolisi gets a quick nail trim. Despite appearances, this won’t hurt at all.

UPS Mac
And now, Kolisi’s got a lekker little boot on him.

Voice
The moment of truth… will all the hard work pay off?

UPS Kolisi gets up

Voice
He shakes off his grogginess… success!!

There’s still a long road ahead, but it’s one Pierre is happy to stay on..

UPS Dr Pierre Bester
It’s a privilege to work with these animals. If you get to know rhinos, they’re intelligent, they’re soft, they’re gentle.

Voice
Ultimately, the END goal is to see orphans like little Mpho back in the wild.

UPS Arrie
We rescue, we raise, we rehabilitate and we release.

Voice
Before our trip ends…one final question. Mahlatsi’s arrival means Mpho finally has a rhino friend her own size. But would the two orphans hit it off?

UPS Mpho and Mahlatsi meet

Voice
A miracle made possible by the dedicated work of caregivers like Yolande and team.

UPS Arrie
They are absolute rhino angels, they save them, not me. 

Voice
The unexpected trio is adapting to their new routine - a makeshift family for the foreseeable future.

One more battle won… in an ongoing war.

UPS Arrie
And it’s a massive war and we are fighting organised crime. But we cannot lose this war. There’s no way we are going to lose this fight. Never. I will not lose a species on my watch.



PROMO1
 
VO
At an undisclosed location in the middle of the bush, we meet an unlikely pair of friends…
 
Upsound Arrie van Deventer
Arrie: She keeps Mpho company. And she’s a freaking character, you’ve seen her, she thinks she runs the place, she’s the queen bee here.

VO
A dynamic duo who have turned the tables on a South African tragedy.
 
 
 
 
PROMO2

UPS MAC 
Makazole Mapimpi! Hello baby!
 
VO
We meet a different kind of Springbok team in the middle of nowhere…

UPS MAC
It’s a tough job out here hey

VO
And witness a unique solution for an injured captain

UPS MAC
And now Kolisi’s got a lekker little boot on him.

 
 
 
PROMO3

VO
One is a crazy Pedi sheep, the other a five month old rhino orphan - and they are besties.
 
UPS MPHO GETTING SCRATCH
Mac: Look at her, look at her
 
VO
Meet the dynamic duo who refuse to let tragic beginnings get them down.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Unexpected Bedfellows: At a secret location in the middle of the South African bush, we meet the most unexpected of bedfellows, Mpho and Flenters. One is an orphaned rhino calf, the other a sheep. The
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have behind the scenes access to the Rhino Orphanage - a non profit organisation that saves orphaned rhinos, often after their mother's fell victim to poachers. Young rhino are completely incapable of caring for themselves if they lose their mother's, and will either fall prey to predators such as lions or eat dirt in an attempt to survive, which will lead to a tragic death. The Rhino Orphanage specialises in saving these orphans - they have trained K9's who can track the animals, and dedicated carers who work around the clock to keep them alive when they're first brought in. One such case happened in June this year, when they saved their latest addition, Mpho. Because Mpho is still too young to be placed with other rhinos, and they don't want her to get too used to humans, she's been given a companion animal - Flenter's the sheep. The two are getting along like a house on fire, and with Flenter's help Mpho should one day be able to return to the bush.
metadata.Summary: Mpho and Flenters are the stars of our show - and we'll focus on getting amazing footage of their unique bond. As their story unwinds, we'll meet all the role players behind the orphanage, find out how they started, and why they do what they do. There are many other orphans to meet - quite a few of them named after Springbok rugby players. Each with their own tale of tragedy turned healing. One such Rhino calf is Impi, who will be having a specially fabricated prosthetic leg fitted while we are there. Impi and his mother spent two days fighting off a pride of lions before they were saved. Both were badly injured during the encounter. No one is sure if the prosthetic will work, but we'll capture the moment. While the scourge of rhino poaching is a devastating reality in South Africa, and one we won't ignore in the insert, this story is really about Mpho and Flenters, and in true South African tradition, about how the most diverse of backgrounds can lead to inspiring friendships.
metadata.Further information: We have been granted access to everything and everyone at the orphanage, and they are happy to help. I have agreed not to disclose the location.
